Hi Sam -

Thanks for the productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Recap
- Primary goal: embed high-quality long-form summarization in FinWave’s analyst workflow with sub-1s token latency for short queries and predictable throughput for batch jobs.
- Data sensitivity: PII redaction required, logs stored in customer KMS.
- Current infra: CPU-first inference for prototyping, looking to move to GPU-backed dedicated capacity for production.

Immediate recommendations (high level)
1) Run a short model-fit evaluation across 3 variants: 7B -> AWQ 4-bit, 13B -> GPTQ 4-bit, 13B -> FP8 (mixed-precision) to measure quality delta on your prompt set and throughput/cost.
2) Baseline prompts: we’ll use the prompt-set we discussed (intent+examples). Please find attached the initial prompt_set_v1.jsonl and a one-pager of the recommended eval plan.
3) Timeline: 2 weeks for dev-run evals, then a production-grade perf run if results look good.

Next steps
- I’ll kick off the eval run with Dev and Nikhil once you confirm which three models you want prioritized.
- Can you share the 10 representative documents for the eval (anonymized) and confirm procurement contact for contract timeline?

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (prompt seeds), quant-tradeoff-notes.pdf (plan)

Thanks - happy to jump on a quick follow-up if useful.

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & quantization trade-offs (FinWave)

Sam - thanks, answers inline and with more detail below.

Short summary: expected quality vs throughput trade-offs (13B)
- FP8 (mixed-precision): smallest quality delta vs fp16 baseline - typically <1-2% on ROUGE/BERTScore for summarization, highest throughput uplift for FP8-optimized kernels, but requires hardware/runtime support (NVIDIA H100 class or similar).
- GPTQ-4 (post-training quant): good throughput, moderate quality delta (~2-4% on our summarization tests). Stable across many families but can show brittle failure modes on rare token sequences; recommended with a light calibration set.
- AWQ-4 (activation-aware quant): often the best throughput/quality balance for recent transformer variants - throughput near GPTQ but with smaller regressive quality impact on complex prompts (~1-3%). Strong candidate for production if you need aggressive cost savings and lower latency.

Tradeoffs we’ll measure in the eval run
- Quality: ROUGE/L, BERTScore, and a custom hallucination check (precision of facts extracted vs source).
- Latency: p50/p95 for single-request patterns and batch throughput (tokens/sec) for bulk jobs.
- Cost: estimated $/1M tokens for each quant+model config on a Dedicated pool.

Links and evidence
- Public trade study (Redwood): https://redwood-inference.github.io/benchmarks/awq-gptq-fp8
- Internal benchmark summary (attached): benchmark-results-summary.csv
- Prompt set attached: prompt-set-v1.jsonl

Proposed eval plan (week 1-2)
1) Week 1: Dev-run - 10 anonymized reports, run 3 model variants (13B-FP8, 13B-GPTQ4, 13B-AWQ4). Collect quality metrics and latency.
2) Week 2: Production perf run - if results look good, run larger set (200 docs) to validate throughput/cost and run a canary on a Dedicated pool.

Procurement / SOW
- I’ll draft a short SOW (scope, data handling, timelines) and share with procurement@finwave.com - expect within 48 hours. For budgeting, ballpark Dedicated pool for 200 concurrent requests (mixed small/large queries) is $XXk/month; I’ll provide a detailed estimate in the SOW.

Attachments: benchmark-results-summary.csv, quant-tradeoff-notes.pdf, prompt-set-v1.jsonl

Let me know if you prefer a different model family in the matrix (we can substitute a 7B option if you want a cheaper baseline).

Best,
Marissa
